_doc: HAUSSMANN P0.5 (editorial gate, O1) — the B5 claim register as a CI fixture. Source of record: how/campaigns/campaign_haussmann/evidence/claims/claim_register.md (126 unique ids across 140 table rows, derived by script at P4.5a §9.5) + claims_raw.json (live fetch 2026-08-16). This fixture is the machine-checkable SLICE. Its composition CHANGED at P1.1 and this line lagged two missions: it described 'all 8 FALSE rows (the launch blockers) + 12 representative verified rows', but P1.1 resolved the FALSE set 8/8 and the rows were cleaned out, so the slice is now 26 rows, ALL verified, ZERO FALSE — currency canaries only. The FALSE machinery in gate-26 is retained deliberately for the next false claim, not because one is pinned here. KNOWN COVERAGE GAP (P4.5a, filed for P4.4): this gate cannot express 'a retired claim must stay gone' for a row that was never FALSE. FALSE rows are transient by design — they carry expected_fail_until and go RED as an unexpected pass the moment they are fixed — so an `unsupported -> cut` row like R-121 or R-125 has no permanent absence assertion here. R-125 and R-120 are guarded by dedicated assertions in gate-23 instead; R-121 is guarded indirectly, by pinning the LABEL that replaced the invention.
_relation_to_gate_20: gate-20 traces claims to their SOURCE FILES (does `vaults.json` still say 74?). This fixture asserts the RENDERED PAGE — that a false sentence is gone, and that a true one has not silently vanished. Different failure modes, no overlap: the G-01..G-10 accessor rows stay in claim_trace_manifest.json and are deliberately NOT duplicated here.
_quote_rule: Every `quote` is the exact page-visible text, verified against the 2026-08-16 build snapshot. Comparison normalizes typography only (curly quotes -> straight, em/en dash -> hyphen, whitespace collapsed) so a smart-quote change cannot fake a pass or a fail. `match_in: html` rows assert against raw markup instead (attributes, hrefs).
_no_count_pinning: Campaign convention 8 (WebForge KW-8/FR-K): verified quotes are trimmed to their non-numeric clause wherever a count appears, so this gate never pins live registry data. Count currency is gate-21's job, count provenance is gate-20's.

rows.quote: aDNA (agentic DNA) is an open standard for organizing a project's files
rows.why: The ADR-048 definition-as-hero lead (ratified DP2; shipped P1.1) — the anti-jargon functional definition, spec public + versioned + MIT, clone-and-run image real. Replaced the Meridian-era 'project knowledge' phrasing.

rows.quote: Every file is plain Markdown. Browse in Obsidian, VS Code, or GitHub. No proprietary formats, no lock-in.
rows.why: The no-lock-in promise. Verifiable by cloning the image; must not silently disappear in a redesign.

rows.quote: The connections are not decorative. Each line is a relationship a vault actually declares
rows.why: The graph's honesty caption — it is what makes a sparse topology a feature rather than an embarrassment.

rows.quote: never leave the computer unless you send them
rows.why: The local-first privacy claim (Standing Rule 4). A high-consequence promise: if the architecture ever changes, this sentence must change with it.

rows.quote: MIT-licensed and versioned in public; the spec is the source of truth.
rows.why: Openness claim that IS true today — the contrast case for R-20. Keeping it asserted proves the gate is not simply hostile to openness language.

rows.quote: aDNA is stewarded today by one person
rows.why: The scale-honesty stratum the campaign exists to protect. The single most disarming sentence on the site; a growth-minded rewrite would delete it first.

rows.quote: The workspace is files on your machine and makes no network calls of its own.
rows.why: The privacy promise at the point of install, where it actually matters. RE-PINNED A SECOND TIME at HAUSSMANN GR-1 O5 (2026-08-28), and this time the CLAIM changed, not just the wording: the S3 caveat this row had carried since P0.5 — that the required agent tool sends prompts and file contents to its provider — is now STATED ON THE PAGE rather than held only in the register. The old sentence scoped, as written, over a command ending `&& claude`. First re-pin was P4.5b O2 (2026-08-26), wording only, lives-on -> stays-on for ADR-048 §50. Note what this row was doing before that: gate-26 asserts verified quotes are PRESENT, so the register was pinning the one phrasing the voice rule forbids. A claim register locks in wording as well as truth — and it can also hold a diagnosis whose remedy nobody ships, which is what happened here for eleven missions.

rows.quote: This site is itself an aDNA vault
rows.why: The self-conformance proof (directive law 2). If this stops being true the site has refuted its own standard. Quote re-pinned at HAUSSMANN P4.5b O1 (2026-08-26): the rewrite dropped the word 'documentation'. The CLAIM is unchanged and still verified — site source is in the public aDNA-Network/aDNA.aDNA repo under site/ — so this is a same-diff re-pin, not a weakening.

rows.quote: not real named adopters
rows.why: Honesty stratum: the disclaimer that keeps illustrative personas from reading as customer logos. Its removal would be a silent credibility regression.

rows.quote: not a certified
rows.why: Honesty stratum: the disclaimer that stops the compliance page reading as an accreditation. Sits on the same page as the FALSE R-84 — this gate protects one while condemning the other.

rows.quote: Archive, never delete
rows.why: A real, checkable governance control (Standing Order 6) on the auditor-facing page — the honest counterpart to R-84's false control claim.

rows.quote: that is honest topology, not missing data
rows.why: The house style in one clause: an unflattering fact stated plainly. Quote trimmed of its leading count so this row cannot pin live registry data.

rows.quote: Language and DNA were co-created by everyone before us. The context that powers AI should be too - built, shared, and governed in the open, for the good of all.
rows.why: The manifesto lyric, demoted INTACT from the hero to the movement band per ADR-048 ('demoted intact to the movement band directly below the fold'). Its silent deletion would violate the ratified package.

rows.quote: registration is approval-gated, so joining is a request an operator reviews, not a click
rows.why: The honest-state disclosure on the community-space link (ADR-054 copy law; link-GO fired by operator ruling 2026-08-17, promotion GO at DP7 2026-08-22). Re-probed [D 2026-08-22]: app_public.registration.mode='approval'. REWRITTEN AT P3.4 — the prior quote ('...its terms of service, privacy policy, and branding are still being stood up') was stamped `verified` on 2026-08-17 evidence and went FALSE on 2026-08-21 when both policies went live. Because this gate asserts `verified` quotes are PRESENT, the suite was green BECAUSE of the false sentence and would have gone red on the truth. No row here carries a probe date, so nothing could catch it: convention 15's stale-row blind spot, with an instrument defending the stale claim. The branding clause is dropped rather than restated, per the DP7 ruling that the instance's public face is an upstream ceiling the site neither describes nor claims.

rows.quote: All of them run on one computer, operated by one person
rows.why: The sentence the whole campaign turns on (hypothesis H5, the trust stratum's only S1; anti-pattern 7.3 inverted by disclosure). A synthetic cold-reader reached this conclusion unaided and concluded the network was one org cosplaying as an ecosystem — the fix is to say it first, plainly. This is the single row most likely to be deleted by a growth-minded rewrite, and its deletion would restore the exact defect the disclosure surface exists to cure.

rows.quote: No number on this page is typed by hand.
rows.why: Structurally true via src/data/network_state.ts, and machine-checked by the gate-20 manifest rows — which is what makes it a guarantee rather than a promise. If anyone ever hardcodes a count on this page, this sentence becomes a lie, so the row is the tripwire for that.

rows.quote: Every public property aDNA operates or vouches for is on this list.
rows.why: The completeness claim that makes the properties page a defense rather than a list (instrument 7.1). SCOPED at O3: the original said 'Everything legitimate is on this list', which the page contradicted 40 lines later ('Not every repository under our organization is listed') and which /about contradicted by linking stanley.science. A completeness claim that documents its own exceptions spends credibility to buy nothing. Enforced by the gate-15 G6b set-equality assertions.

rows.quote: aDNA runs no social accounts. Any account using the name is not us.
rows.why: True today: SocialLinks.astro is imported nowhere and no handle exists in site/src. TIGHTENED at O3: the original added 'There is no aDNA account on any social platform' — a universal negative about every platform on earth that we cannot know, a reader cannot check, and the very next sentence assumed the opposite of. KNOWN EXPIRY: the day an aDNA account is opened, this row must be updated in the same diff as the copy.

rows.quote: the person who operates this network also holds a role at the Foundation
rows.why: The related-party disclosure, added at O3 after a hostile read found the page calling the Wilhelm Foundation independent while /about named the operator as Head of AI there. Without it the 'What is not ours' section did credibility work it had not earned, and a reader comparing the two pages would have found the conflict the site itself supplied — which reads as selective disclosure and costs more than the fact it hides. Deleting this sentence restores that defect.

rows.quote: The honest starting point is the one above: one named architect, one anchor partner whose closeness to this project we named rather than hid, public-good work shown row by row with what you can open today
rows.why: The /about closing band, rewritten at the P1.2 close after the re-rank (finding F1) caught it re-asserting 'a real Founding Architect, a real anchor partner, real public-good work' fifty lines below the band THIS MISSION rebuilt to stop asserting exactly that (R-62). Same claim family as R-28, which was lowered on / but never adjudicated on its /about sibling. This is the family's SECOND recurrence, which is why it is pinned: band 4 shows the state row by row, and the closing band must not assert past it. The cut clause 'Real stewards grow the network' asserted stewards the same page says do not exist yet.

rows.quote: If you found something claiming to be aDNA that is not on this list
rows.why: The exits section added at the P1.2 close after the re-rank (finding F2) — both reviewer lenses independently found that this page dead-ended at the footer while its twin, built in the same mission and sharing its scaffold, closed with five real exits. Pinned because the reader who has just satisfied themselves the site is genuine is at the point of highest intent, and routing that intent to the security-reporting path is the whole operational value of a clone-site defense. Deleting the exits restores the dead end the 2.50 Actionability score measured.

rows.quote: which is not 74 live projects
rows.why: The /vaults hero sentence authored at P2.4 (ADR-052 §tiers). It exists to disarm the reading a bare count invites — anti-pattern 7.4, quantity of entries is not evidence of network health — in the first line a stranger reads rather than in a caveat further down. Pinned on the CLAUSE, not the numbers: campaign convention 8 (KW-8/FR-K) forbids pinning counts, and the surrounding figures are interpolated from vaults.json at build time, so a 75th vault must not turn this row red. gate-35 asserts the counts themselves against the registry.

rows.quote: These stages are self-declared
rows.why: ADR-052 §tiers.2 calls this the single most important caveat on the registry surface, and the measurement behind it is stark: github_url populated on 1 of 74 rows, docs_site_url on 0, last_synced on 24 with 18 sharing one date. There is genuinely nothing to check a declared stage against. Pinned because the tier badges make the registry look MORE authoritative than it was before, and this sentence is the entire counterweight — losing it silently would leave the badges asserting an assessment nobody performed. gate-35 additionally asserts it is body text and not a title attribute.

rows.quote: Related-party disclosure: the person who operates this network also holds a role at the Foundation
rows.why: HAUSSMANN P4.5a. R-111's live scope after re-probe (register §9.7) was /canonical-properties ALONE — the disclosure had already shipped on /about and /state-of-the-network, and the register row overstated the gap for two missions because it was never re-probed. This is the sharp half: the page whose entire job is 'here is how you check we are who we say we are' filed the Wilhelm Foundation under 'not ours' while two sibling pages disclosed that the operator holds a role there. Deleting this sentence restores selective disclosure on the one page a skeptical reader checks. Paired with the existing R-111 row, which guards the half that shipped at P1.2 — same finding, two faces.

rows.quote: not a case study, and no measured project is being described
rows.why: HAUSSMANN P4.5a. The 'Before and after' section asserted a lab's 200 files and a three-day onboarding with no lab, no date and no source — an unlabelled hypothetical in the site's own voice, found by a cold reader one mission after the campaign cut a fabrication and published why. Fixed the way R-118 was: invented specifics cut AND the nature of the claim labelled, because cutting the numbers while leaving 'a lab's' would still imply an observed case. This quote is that label; deleting it lets the section drift back toward reading as reportage.

rows.quote: August 20, 2026
rows.why: HAUSSMANN P4.5a. changelog.astro formatted entry dates with toLocaleDateString and no timeZone, so a UTC-midnight frontmatter date rendered in the BUILD MACHINE's zone — every entry displayed one day early from a PDT build, and correctly from a UTC one. The rendered date was a function of where the build ran, while the same <time> element's datetime attribute was always right, so the machine-readable and human-readable dates disagreed on one line. Pinned as the regression canary: if timeZone:'UTC' is ever dropped, the 2026-08-20 entry renders as August 19 and this row goes red. Not a count pin — changelog entries are static content, not live registry data.

rows.quote: your content is not used to train or evaluate AI models, and every agent in the space is labeled as an agent
rows.why: Both clauses are quoted commitments from the documents this block links, verified at source [D 2026-08-22]: privacy.md §2 'Your content is not used to train or evaluate AI models.' and code_of_conduct.md §3 'Every agent is visibly labeled as an agent.' + 'No undisclosed automation.' Framed as commitments IN THE RULES, not as independently observed facts — what happens inside the venue is behind the auth wall. Satisfies Fluxer SO#8 (agents always disclosed) without asserting a presence this desk cannot verify. Replaces the P1.1 sentence 'agents work in the repositories and on the public record, not in chat', which aDNALabs S224 ruling 2 (2026-08-21, 'Fluxer = human-visible agent chat') falsified and which the linked code of conduct §3 directly contradicts.

rows.quote: Anything that should leave a durable record
rows.why: The question-path routing ADR-054 clause 2 requires (AC2). States the venue/repository division WITHOUT naming GitHub Discussions, which is not enabled — that was R-46, the S1 FALSE row whose resolution re-routed the funnel to this venue. AC2 as written asked for a 'venue vs Discussions' division, i.e. a division against a venue that does not exist; corrected here. Consistent with the page's ClosingCTA and proposals section rather than competing with them.

rows.quote: no server, no signup; aDNA itself sends nothing
rows.why: ADR-048's NOT-line, ⛩ AMENDED AND SCOPED AT R-97 (2026-09-04). It read '…nothing leaves your machine' — an unscoped absolute that is FALSE for the reader's own tooling, since the agentic coding tool the audience sub names sends prompts to its provider. This string is R-64's P0.5 PRESCRIPTION verbatim ("scope it to 'aDNA itself sends nothing'"), and R-97 is the FIRST surface to ship it: GR-1 discharged R-64 on /get-started with a DIFFERENT string ('makes no network calls of its own'), and 'itself sends nothing' measured 0 occurrences across the built site before this commit [D 2026-09-04]. Fourth surface the campaign has scoped (R-64 /get-started · R-161 /network · R-167 /privacy · R-97 /); NOT claimed to be the last — R-33 was already correctly scoped pre-campaign, and whether any unscoped absolute remains is unmeasured, since the ⛩ scope ruling declined a sweep (convention 16: a claim no wider than the command that produced it). ⭐ THIS ROW EXISTS BECAUSE IT DID NOT: R-97 was classed `verified` in the register and asserted by NOTHING — absent from this fixture (28 rows), absent from claim_trace_manifest.json, and present in gate-23 only as a comment [D 2026-09-04]. gate-26's contract is 'verified rows must be PRESENT', so the register's strongest class had a hole at the site's most-read sentence — convention 18's family, where a gate's green is a true statement about a set that excludes the claim. Trimmed to the operative clause per the _quote_rule and convention 8: a partial revert of the tail alone still reds this row, which is the failure mode worth catching.
